newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Short Australian debt futures ease, RBA quiet.
newsitem.headline: Short Australian debt futures ease, RBA quiet.

text.p: *Short Australian debt futures weakened after the RBA made no announcement on policy after Tuesday's board meeting with the market having set itself up for a surprise easing.
*RBA's Macfarlane faces parliamentary committee on Thursday.
Short Australian debt futures weakened after the Reserve Bank of Australia made no announcement on policy after Tuesday's board meeting.
While the chances of an easing were seen as slim after last week's stronger than expected wages data, the market had positioned itself for a surprise easing, traders said.

By 9.45 a.m. (2345 GMT) June bill futures had slipped to 94.03, having stood at around 94.08 at 9.30 a.m. when the central bank's usually makes announcements on policy. At its current level, the contract is roughly in line with current 6.0 percent official interest rates.
The focus now switches to Thursday's labour force report and RBA governor Ian Macfarlane's testimony to a parliamentary finance committee.
Employment is forecast to rebound by 35,000 after its recent weak trend, while unemployment is seen sticking at 8.7 percent, according to a Reuters survey of economists.

"If that (the data) doesn't rebound, then people will be watching the comments from Macfarlane very carefully to see if they have any concerns at all about growth being too soft, and the monetary policy speculation can come back at some point," said Stephen Roberts, chief economist at UBS Australia.

The market reversed its initial spread tightening against the dollar bloc after the RBA left policy unchanged. U.S. and Canadian debt had softened on Tuesday following a weak response to a three-year U.S. note auction, while N.Z. bonds were also under pressure from a fall in the N.Z. TWI.
